obligations.note: The change adds 'coapplicant_tax_id' to ApplicantFields.ALL but does NOT add it to NpiRegistry.FIELDS (the closed domain that drives encryption). A tax identifier is explicitly NPI per the obligation statement ('government identifiers such as SSN or tax id'). Because it is absent from the NPI registry, CaseStore will not seal it at rest, and the exhaustive control test (which enumerates NpiRegistry.FIELDS) cannot detect the gap. The field will be persisted in plaintext.

Retention.purge() now explicitly calls removeApplicantField('coapplicant_tax_id') in addition to iterating NpiRegistry.FIELDS, so the new NPI field is purged. The legal-hold and retention-period logic is unchanged; the sample retention test passes.

summary: The change introduces a 'coapplicant_tax_id' field (a government tax identifier, which is NPI under the bank's own definition in ENC-1) into the applicant data model, but it is not added to NpiRegistry.FIELDS. Consequently CaseStore will not seal it at rest, and the exhaustive control test that enumerates the registry will not detect the gap. This is a critical violation of ENC-1 (NPI encrypted at rest). All process obligations (CHG-1 through CHG-7, EXC-1, LAP-1) and RET-1 are satisfied, but the encryption-at-rest violation is sufficient to reject the change. The PR should be returned to engineering to add 'coapplicant_tax_id' to NpiRegistry.FIELDS (and update the NPI field list in policy-params.json) so that the field is sealed on persistence and the control test actually exercises it.
